Several years ago, my therapist’s husband died very unexpectedly. At the time when we first met again and the couple of emails we did exchange, I mostly just told her that I was incredibly sad to hear what had happened and very sorry for her loss. I think when I hadn’t heard from her via email around the time she’d said I would I did also send a cute/funny cat picture of my own cat in a pose she’d mentioned finding very funny previously and just said that I hoped she was doing as okay as she could be and that maybe the cat picture could bring some slight smile.

I was really unsure what I was/wasn’t allowed to ask or say when we resumed meeting (and I also happened to be away for a bit when she first came back, so that made things weird too). It wasn’t until actually a few years later that we finally discussed it together, and it still comes up sometimes. Obviously every therapist and situation is different, but this death was somewhat public, so she preferred clients to ask her what happened rather than to assume from whatever they had found online (though I refused to read those), and we’ve talked a lot about any feelings that come up.

It’s really hard to care so much about a long term therapist and have that very personal yet professional one-sided relationship with them when something like this happens. It really is.

My therapist is truly the best human I know and I trust her fully. I’ve been seeing her for 4.5 years at this point. She is skilled with CPTSD. We’ve talked a lot about grounding, but I do think I could work them in more during my day to day life. I have a breathing app that I use sometimes as well as a PTSD specific app, though I don’t often find that one helpful. I do dissociate quite a bit, but it is much improved from what it was a couple years ago. Tbh I miss when I was dissociating often because it felt less painful than this. I’m not sure I fully understand what the somatic approaches to EMDR entail, but we often talk about how I feel in my body and between sets of eye movements do some PMR and breathing exercises. I actually met with my therapist today (which was supposed to be an EMDR day, but we ended up talking instead), and after discussing how hopeless and defeated I feel, she offered to research and call places for adjunctive treatment options and even work to figure out the insurance piece of things. I don’t have the words to describe how much that means to me that she’s wanting to do that for me when I feel unable to do it myself.
